notes: This record applies the owner's decision kb/Work R43 item 3 (2026-09-24: a rule whose trigger can only arise through an unsupported capability, multi-reel files named, closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT, to be re-adjudicated if the capability is added), the ground on which the 2023 rule this row maps to (GR-14.9.30.4-23) is held; it makes no new decision, and the orchestrator should confirm that the decision covers this 1985 row before it is applied. §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR9 acts only when "during the execution of a READ statement, the end of reel/unit is recognized or a reel/unit contains no logical records, and the logical end of the file has not been reached": the ending label procedure, "A reel/unit swap. The current volume pointer is updated to point to the next reel/unit existing for the file.", and the beginning label procedure. No file of this implementation has a second reel or unit, at any edition (no edition arm): a connector resolves one host path, SequentialConnector.Category answers PhysicalFileCategory.NonUnit (§1985:VII.4.2.4 GR2 a: "A file whose input or output medium is such that the concepts of rewind and reels/units have no meaning"), and SequentialConnector.ReadRecord has one end, the end of the file, where it answers status 10; it has no end-of-reel arm, no volume pointer and no label procedure. The 1985 text lets a reel device go unsupported (§1985:I.1.5.2.5.1: "Language elements that pertain to specific hardware components for which support is not claimed need not be implemented. The absence of such elements from an implementation of Standard COBOL must be specified."; §1985:C.3 lists the REEL/UNIT phrase of CLOSE as dependent on a reel or mass storage type of device), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md states the absence ("No reel/unit device is provided", A.3 items 28 to 30 and DOC-A.1-24), citing the 2023 clauses only. The witness shows the documented posture: CLOSE ... REEL on the output file leaves it open (FileRegistry.CloseReelUnit), the records written before and after it form one file, and the READ loop delivers both and then the at end condition with no swap. Probed further at --std 85: CLOSE REEL and CLOSE UNIT FOR REMOVAL answer status 07 (§1985:VII.1.3.5: "the referenced file is on a non-reel/unit medium") on an output file and on an input file in mid-read, and the next READ delivers the next record of the same file.
